features.description: The A1 plan: how `notify` learns `kind=`/`feature=`, builds the v1 event in node, posts it to EVENT_URL through the stub curl and falls back to ntfy, with every call site mapped to its kind and every check named before any code is written.
steps: `docs/plans/2026-11-07-A1-event-hook.md` exists with one section per build feature (A1-02 the event builder in lib/notify.mjs and the routed post in lib/notify.sh; A1-03 the call sites' `kind=`/`feature=` fields, the decision file, the docs lines and the folded review), each naming the files it edits and the checks it writes first, each check with its tier by journal/decisions/2026-11-03-suite-tiers.md's 30 s rule.

The plan states the event JSON exactly as tests/fixtures/n8n-event-v1.json has it (the same keys in the same order, `v` 1) and who fills each key: `id` from node's `crypto.randomUUID()`, `at` ISO 8601, `project` the state dir's project name, `run` RUN_ID, `feature` the `feature=` field or null, `priority` the ntfy value or "", `click`/`actions` the ntfy values or null, `context` null until A2; and that the `debrief` kind gives null `project`, `run` and `feature`.

The plan states the POST verbatim: `${HARNESS_CURL:-curl}` with `-H "Content-Type: application/json"`, `--max-time "$EVENT_TIMEOUT"`, no `--retry`, never an `Authorization` header, how the HTTP code is read (`-w '%{http_code}'` or `--fail`'s exit, the plan's choice), the two lines verbatim (`event → n8n: <kind> <id>` by `log`; `event hook failed (<code or curl exit>): <kind>; sent to ntfy` by `note`, by `log` where the caller has no `note`, as lib/debrief.sh), and what tests/stub-curl.sh gains to answer the event POST a 200 (default), a 500 and a timeout, each knob in the stub's header and every error line copied from real curl output into tests/fixtures/ (never invented).

The plan maps every `notify` call to its kind in one table: lib/record.sh `notify_park` → park; `needs_you` and the merge-refused `needs_notify` → needs_michael; lib/driver.sh's run-end notify → blocked when `ehigh` is 1, else ended; its `started`, `paused` and deploy-guard lines; lib/record.sh's merged; lib/lane.sh's limit line; lib/debrief.sh's headline → debrief and its `fail()` → other; lib/desk.sh and bin/harness's continue-refused → needs_michael or other; and it says how `needs_notify` (lib/needs.sh) forwards `kind=` and `feature=` to `notify`.

The plan lists every existing check whose curl.log or notify-cmd.log assertion the new fields or the stub's new knobs could change (`grep -ln 'curl_\|notify-cmd' tests/checks/*.sh`), each marked `stays` or with its replacement's name, and names the checks A1 adds: in tests/checks/event-hook.sh (fast; lib/notify.sh sourced the way tests/checks/notify-body-cap.sh does), in tests/checks/event-run.sh (slow; stub runs) and in tests/unit/notify.test.mjs, with the storage path `<STATE_ROOT>/events/<id>/event.json` and retention left to A2.
`bash tests/run.sh --tier fast` ends with every check passing (its `N/N checks passed` line); the suite is green.

features.description: `notify` accepts `kind=` and `feature=`; with EVENT_URL set a park, needs_michael, blocked or debrief kind is POSTed as v1 event JSON (built by `lib/notify.mjs event`) through the stub curl, a 2xx ends there with a log line, anything else notes the failure and sends the ntfy post byte for byte as today; unset EVENT_URL changes nothing.
steps: Written first and watched failing, in tests/unit/notify.test.mjs (flat `test("notify.mjs event: …")` calls): `buildEvent` returns an object whose `Object.keys` equal tests/fixtures/n8n-event-v1.json's keys in order; `v` is 1; `id` matches `^[0-9a-f-]{36}$`; `at` parses with `Date.parse`; an empty click, actions or context becomes null and an empty priority stays ""; a `debrief` kind gives null `project`, `run` and `feature`; `node lib/notify.mjs event kind=park run=r1 project=p feature=B title=t body=b priority=high click= actions=` prints that JSON; each name in tests/fixtures/check-names.txt and check-names-fast.txt (LC_ALL=C sorted).

Written first and watched failing, in tests/checks/event-hook.sh (line 2 `# tier: fast`; lib/notify.sh sourced in a subshell with `log` and `note` appending to files, NTFY_URL and NTFY_TOKEN=tok-secret-123 set as tests/lib.sh's base config has them): (a) EVENT_URL unset, `notify x kind=park` → one stub-curl call, to the ntfy URL; (b) EVENT_URL=https://n8n.example/webhook/harness-event, kind=park, stub 200 → exactly one call, to EVENT_URL, with `Content-Type: application/json` among its arguments, its `--data-binary` body parsing with `jq -e '.v == 1 and .kind == "park" and .feature == "B"'`, no `Authorization` argument and no `tok-secret-123` anywhere in $T/curl.log, no call to the ntfy URL, and the log file holding `event → n8n: park <id>` (`grep -F`); (c) stub 500 → the POST, then an ntfy call whose argument list equals (a)'s record of curl.log byte for byte (`diff`), and the note `event hook failed (500): park; sent to ntfy`; (d) stub timeout → the same with `event hook failed (curl exit 28): park; sent to ntfy`; (e) EVENT_URL set, kind=ended → ntfy only, (a)'s record again; (f) no `kind=` → ntfy only; (g) `notify` returns 0 in (b), (c) and (d); (h) after (b) `$HARNESS_STATE/events/<id>/event.json` exists and equals the posted body; (i) the event's `title`, `body`, `click`, `actions` and `priority` in (c) equal the ntfy call's `Title:`, data, `Click:`, `Actions:` and `Priority:` values.

lib/config.sh's `harness_config` sets `EVENT_URL=""` and `EVENT_TIMEOUT=5` beside NTFY_URL with one comment; templates/user/config.sh gains a commented `# EVENT_URL=` and `# EVENT_TIMEOUT=5` under Notifications with one-line comments (what is routed, the fallback); `grep -c EVENT_URL lib/config.sh templates/user/config.sh` prints at least 1 for each file.

lib/notify.sh: `notify` parses `kind=` and `feature=` like its other fields (no kind is `other`); only park, needs_michael, blocked and debrief with a non-empty EVENT_URL go through `ask notify.mjs event …` (no JSON written in bash), are kept at `${HARNESS_STATE:-…}/events/<id>/event.json`, and are POSTed with `--max-time "$EVENT_TIMEOUT"`, no `--retry` and no token; a 2xx logs `event → n8n: <kind> <id>` and returns 0 without any ntfy or NOTIFY_CMD call; every other outcome notes `event hook failed (…): <kind>; sent to ntfy` and runs today's branch unchanged; its usage header names the two fields and the routing; `bash -n lib/notify.sh` and `node --check lib/notify.mjs` pass.

tests/stub-curl.sh answers the event POST per the plan's knobs (200 by default; a 500 and a timeout, exit 28, under knobs its header names), the error lines copied from real curl output into tests/fixtures/ (one file each, named in the stub's header); the existing STUB_CURL_FAIL=1 path is unchanged and `bash tests/run.sh notify-body-cap origin-outage needs-record` ends green.
`bash tests/run.sh event-hook unit-tier` ends with every check passing (its `N/N checks passed` line).
`bash tests/run.sh --tier fast` ends with every check passing (its `N/N checks passed` line); the suite is green.

features.description: Every notification names its kind at its call site (park, needs_michael, blocked, debrief, ended, verified, merged, started, paused, limit, other), proven on stub runs with EVENT_URL set; the A1 decision file and the architecture and README lines; an Opus subagent reviews the A1 diff.
steps: Written first and watched failing, in tests/checks/event-run.sh (line 2 `# tier: slow`): with `EVENT_URL=https://n8n.example/webhook/harness-event` appended to $T/user-config.sh and the stub answering 200, a stub run whose coding session parks a feature (the knob tests/checks/park-desk.sh uses) posts exactly one event to EVENT_URL with `kind == "park"`, `feature` the parked id, `run` the run id, `project` `proj`, `title` equal to `[<run>] <id> needs you` and `context` null; the run's run.log has `event → n8n: park <id>` (`grep -F`); no ntfy call in $T/curl.log carries that title; the run's harness-log.md has no `event hook failed` line.

In the same file: the same run with the stub answering 500 posts the event, then an ntfy call whose `Title:`, `Priority:`, `Click:`, `Actions:` values and data equal the event's `title`, `priority`, `click`, `actions` and `body` (compared field by field between curl.log and `events/<id>/event.json`), and harness-log.md notes `event hook failed (500): park; sent to ntfy`; a third run with EVENT_URL unset in the config produces a curl.log whose ntfy records for that park equal the fallback run's (diff of the two records with timestamps and the run id normalised).

The plan lists the fixtures A2-02 copies, read-only, from the dj-crate-streaming project (its checkout as bin/harness's `project_dir dj-crate-streaming` resolves it) into tests/fixtures/glossary/ (a `feature_list.json` from one of its `.harness/runs/*`, descriptions cut to 300 characters; the D24-on table of its `docs/decisions.md`, or tests/fixtures/decisions-dj.md extended; a park INBOX.md; a text that mentions `D24`, `N1-01`, `M8`, `D-H1` and a planted `Q99`), each fixture with a one-line provenance in tests/fixtures/glossary/README.md, and what each ID must resolve to (`D-H1` against this repo's journal/decisions.md heading shape `### D-H1 · …`).

The plan states the glossary rules verbatim from docs/specs/2026-10-22-n8n-events.md §A2: features `\b[A-Z]{1,2}\d+-\d+\b`, milestones `\b[A-Z]{1,2}\d+\b` not followed by `-\d`, decisions `\bD\d+\b` and `\bD-H\d+\b` classified before milestones, the sources in order (feature_list.json; the feature list's milestone ids then headings `# M9`, `## 9. M8`, `## H1 · …` in the project's docs; table rows `| D24 | … |` and headings `### D-H1 · …` in CLAUDE.md, README.md, docs/**/*.md, journal/decisions.md and journal/decisions/*.md titles), the first 300 characters markdown-stripped, every match newest file first, `source` as `<path>:<line>`, unresolved never guessed; and the exported function names of lib/glossary.mjs.

The plan states the mechanical move: which functions and lines of lib/debrief.sh (`rec_dir`, `alive`, `fence`, `capped`, `run_context`, `rate_info`, `spend`, `names`, the `{ … } > "$CTX"` block and the CMAX cut) become lib/context.sh's `context_runs <state dir>…` with the same bytes out, what the function takes from its caller (STATE_ROOT, Q, H, LEDGER, SINCE, F, MET), how `harness debrief --dry-run` keeps its output apart from the new `## Glossary` section, and the check that diffs the debrief's dry-run context against `harness context --since <SINCE>`'s context.md with its glossary section cut.

The plan states `harness context <run-id> | --since <YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS> [--out <dir>]` (its lines for bin/harness's header; the default out `<STATE_ROOT>/events/<id>/`; never a `harness report` call), `context.json`'s shape exactly as the spec's block (`v`, `id`, `generated_at`, `scope.runs`, `scope.since`, `runs[]` with `run`, `project`, `ended`, `running`, `features`, `paths` {record, worktree, state, report, inbox, progress}, `summary`, `parked[]`, `open_questions[]`; `glossary[]` with `id`, `kind`, `text`, `source`; `unresolved[]`), which node module builds it (no JSON in bash), the retention rule (events/ entries older than 30 days removed when a new one is written, the check's `touch -d` clock) and the hook's bundle call in lib/notify.sh (bundle before the POST, `context` its absolute path, null plus a note when the bundle fails).

features.description: The bundle gains context.json in the spec's shape, events/ entries older than 30 days are removed when a new one is written, and a routed event's POST carries the bundle's path (written beforehand, so the path exists when n8n reads it; a failed bundle is a note and a null `context`).
steps: Written first and watched failing, in tests/checks/context-bundle.sh: `$T/b1/context.json` passes `jq -e '.v == 1 and (.id | type) == "string" and .generated_at != null and .scope.runs == ["parked"] and .scope.since == null and (.runs | length) == 1 and .runs[0].paths.record != null and .runs[0].parked[0].feature == "B" and ([.glossary[].id] | index("D24")) != null and .unresolved == ["Q99"]'`; `$T/b2/context.json`'s `scope.since` is the time given and `scope.runs` every run since it; `runs[].summary` is null for a run without summary.json and the parsed object otherwise; `runs[].open_questions` carries the parked run's INBOX question text; the JSON is built by node (`grep -c 'jq -n' lib/context.sh` prints 0).

In the same file: with `$HARNESS_STATE/events/old/event.json` touched 31 days back (`touch -d '31 days ago'`) and `events/recent/event.json` one day back, a new bundle written by `harness context parked` removes `old`, keeps `recent`, and says `events: removed 1 bundle older than 30 days` on stdout (and the driver's run notes the same line when the hook writes one).

In tests/checks/event-run.sh: the park event's `context` is an absolute path under `$HARNESS_STATE/events/<id>/` that exists when the POST is made (a `STUB_CURL_SPY` command records `test -f <context>` and `test -f <context dir>/context.json` at call time), its context.json has `scope.runs == [<run>]` and the parked question in `runs[0].open_questions`, and event.json sits beside it; the debrief event's context.json has `scope.runs` equal to the debrief's runs; a bundle forced to fail (the knob the plan names) gives the POST `context: null` and the note `context bundle failed for park; event sent without it`.

lib/notify.sh's routed branch calls lib/context.sh for the bundle before the POST (`--out` the event's directory; the debrief's call scopes it with `--since "$SINCE"`), never `harness report`; `bash -n lib/notify.sh lib/context.sh lib/debrief.sh` passes and `node --check` passes on every `.mjs` touched.

features.description: Review + simplify of A2: an Opus reviewer reads the milestone diff from a file and answers the hard questions (the gatherer's move changed no byte of the debrief's context, the glossary guesses nothing, the bundle can never block or fail a notification); Critical/Important findings fixed RED→GREEN; simplifications applied; the decision file completed; docs as built.

features.description: The A3 plan: the request inbox's validation rules as pure functions, `harness requests`' processing order and files, the backup-window rule, the systemd path unit, and how the suite observes a runner start, with every check named first.
steps: `docs/plans/2026-11-07-A3-request-inbox.md` exists with one section per build feature (A3-02 lib/requests.mjs's validation, result and log-line builders; A3-03 `harness requests` in lib/requests.sh; A3-04 the systemd units, the decision file and the docs lines), each naming the files it edits and the checks it writes first, each with its tier by journal/decisions/2026-11-03-suite-tiers.md's 30 s rule.

The plan states the validation verbatim from docs/specs/2026-10-22-n8n-events.md §A3 (`v == 1`; `id` `^[A-Za-z0-9-]{8,64}$` and not already in `done/`; `verb` answer|continue; `run` `^[A-Za-z0-9._-]+$` and a real run by bin/harness's `state_of`; `text` 1–4000 characters for answer; `brief` at most 2000; no NUL bytes; an unparsable file younger than 10 s left for the next pass, older rejected), the result JSON exactly as the spec's block (`v`, `id`, `at`, `verb`, `run`, `ok`, `exit`, `output` capped at 2000 bytes, `runner_started`, `refused`), the `requests.log` line's fields (time, id, verb, run, ok or refused, exit; never the text) and the rejection texts, each one a string a check greps.

The plan states the processing: `flock` on `requests/.lock`, `*.json` oldest first by mtime then name, `requests/` created mode 700 when missing, `answer` → `"$H" answer "$run" "$text"` as an argv array (no `eval`, no `bash -c`), `continue` → `"$H" queue add --continue "$run"` plus `--brief "$brief"` when given, then `"$H" queue start` unless the local time (the fake clock `HARNESS_NOW` when set) is between 03:15 and 04:30 (`refused: "backup window 03:15–04:30: queued, runner not started"`), the result written to a temp name in `done/` and renamed, the request moved to `done/<id>.request.json` or `rejected/`, and how the suite observes the runner start (tests/lib.sh exports HARNESS_NO_RUNNER=1, which makes `queue_ensure_runner` a silent no-op: the plan says whether the check unsets it for that one call and asserts `tmux has-session -t =h-queue` on the suite's private server, or asserts the result's `runner_started` from `queue start`'s `queue runner started` line).

The plan states the two unit files' content: `systemd/harness-requests.path` (`[Path]` with `DirectoryNotEmpty=%h/.local/state/harness/requests` or `PathExistsGlob=…/*.json`, `Unit=harness-requests.service`, `[Install] WantedBy=default.target`) and `systemd/harness-requests.service` (`Type=oneshot`, `ExecStart=` the repo's `bin/harness requests` by absolute path, `Environment=PATH=` with node's directory), the two install commands for README.md (`systemctl --user link <abs path>/systemd/harness-requests.path <abs path>/systemd/harness-requests.service` then `systemctl --user enable --now harness-requests.path`) and the check that runs `systemd-analyze --user verify` on them when `systemd-analyze` is on PATH and prints PASS with a skipped note otherwise.

The plan names the checks A3 adds in tests/unit/requests.test.mjs and tests/checks/requests-inbox.sh (the answer with quotes, `$(…)`, backticks and newlines landing verbatim in `<state>/inbox.md`; the continue queued and the runner started; the 03:30 refusal; each rejection: unknown verb, unknown run, a `run` holding a parent-directory segment (two dots, a slash, then `x`), text of 4001 characters, `v: 2`, a duplicate id; the young half-written file left alone; `requests.log` free of the answer text; the units verified) and the defaults it records (no third verb, no batching, a continue for a live run accepted as `queue add` accepts it today).
`bash tests/run.sh --tier fast` ends with every check passing (its `N/N checks passed` line); the suite is green.

features.description: lib/requests.mjs: pure, unit-tested rules for the request inbox: validate a request file's text against the v1 contract, decide the backup window from a time, build the result JSON and the requests.log line (never carrying the answer text).
steps: Written first and watched failing, in tests/unit/requests.test.mjs (flat `test("requests.mjs: …")` calls): `validateRequest(text, {runs, done, ageSeconds})` accepts a valid `answer` and a valid `continue` (with and without `brief`); rejects, each with its reason string, `v: 2`, an id of 7 characters, an id with `/`, an id already in `done`, verb `merge`, a run holding a parent-directory segment (two dots, a slash, then `x`), a run not in `runs`, an empty `text`, a text of 4001 characters, a brief of 2001 characters, a text with a NUL byte; returns `wait` for unparsable text with `ageSeconds` 5 and `rejected` with `ageSeconds` 11; `inBackupWindow(date)` is true at 03:15:00 and 04:29:59 local and false at 03:14:59 and 04:30:00; `resultJson` has the spec's ten keys in order with `output` cut to 2000 bytes; `logLine` holds id, verb, run, ok or refused and exit and never the text; each name in tests/fixtures/check-names.txt and check-names-fast.txt (LC_ALL=C sorted).

lib/requests.mjs exists with a one-line usage header, exports `validateRequest`, `inBackupWindow`, `resultJson` and `logLine`, and a CLI (`node lib/requests.mjs validate <file> --runs <list> --done <dir> --now <epoch>` printing the verdict as labelled lines bash reads with `while read -r k v`, as lib/cli.mjs's `labelled`); `node --check lib/requests.mjs` passes; no bash parses request JSON.
`node --test --test-isolation=none tests/unit/*.test.mjs` passes and `bash tests/run.sh unit-tier` ends with every check passing (its `N/N checks passed` line).
`bash tests/run.sh --tier fast` ends with every check passing (its `N/N checks passed` line); the suite is green.

features.description: `harness requests` processes every pending request under flock, oldest first: a valid `answer` reaches `<state>/inbox.md` verbatim through an argv call, a valid `continue` queues the entry and starts the runner except in the 03:15–04:30 window, everything else is rejected; each request leaves a result file, a moved request and one log line without the text.
steps: Written first and watched failing, in tests/checks/requests-inbox.sh (its tier by the 30 s rule; a run state made by tests/lib.sh's `status_stubs`): a request `{"v":1,"id":"req-0001-aaaa","verb":"answer","run":"parked","text":"it's `x` $(rm -rf /) \"q\"\nline two","source":"n8n-card","event":null}` in `$HARNESS_STATE/requests/` makes `harness requests` append exactly that text to `$HARNESS_STATE/proj/parked/inbox.md` (compared with `cmp` against the JSON's `.text` printed by jq), write `requests/done/req-0001-aaaa.json` with `ok == true`, `exit == 0`, `verb == "answer"`, move the request to `requests/done/req-0001-aaaa.request.json`, and add one line to `requests/requests.log` naming the id, `answer`, `parked` and `ok` and not containing `rm -rf`; `requests/` is mode 700 (`stat -c %a`).

In the same file: a `continue` request for `stopped` (proj2) leaves a `$Q/*-continue-stopped.args` entry with `--requested` and its `--brief` text, the result has `runner_started == true` and `refused == null`, and the runner start is observed as docs/plans/2026-11-07-A3-request-inbox.md says (`tmux has-session -t =h-queue` on the suite's private server after unsetting HARNESS_NO_RUNNER for that call, or `queue start`'s `queue runner started` line in `output`); the same request with `HARNESS_NOW` at 03:30 local leaves the entry queued, starts no runner (no `h-queue` session) and its result says `refused == "backup window 03:15–04:30: queued, runner not started"`.

In the same file: six requests (verb `merge`; run `nosuch`; a run holding a parent-directory segment (two dots, a slash, then `x`); a text of 4001 characters; `v: 2`; a second file with id `req-0001-aaaa`) each end in `requests/rejected/` with a result in `done/` whose `ok == false` and `refused` names the reason, and no line reaches any `inbox.md`; a file holding `{"v":1,` alone, 2 s old, is left in place with no result and the next `harness requests` 10 s later (the fake clock) rejects it; a second `harness requests` while one holds `requests/.lock` waits (the first holds it under `flock` for 2 s; both exit 0 and the request is processed once).

lib/requests.sh exists (a one-line usage header; `set -uo pipefail`), bin/harness dispatches `requests` to it and its header has the `harness requests` line (what it reads, writes and never does); the `answer` call is `"$H" answer "$run" "$text"` with no `eval` or `bash -c` anywhere in lib/requests.sh (`grep -c 'eval\|bash -c' lib/requests.sh` prints 0); the result file is written to a temp name and renamed; `bash -n lib/requests.sh bin/harness` passes.

`bash tests/run.sh requests-inbox queue-view` ends with every check passing (its `N/N checks passed` line); every new name is in tests/fixtures/check-names.txt (LC_ALL=C sorted; a fast file's in check-names-fast.txt too).
`bash tests/run.sh --tier fast` ends with every check passing (its `N/N checks passed` line); the suite is green.

features.description: The two systemd user units that run `harness requests` when a request lands, shipped under systemd/ and verified by `systemd-analyze --user verify` where available (never installed by the harness); the A3 decision file and the README and architecture lines.
steps: Written first and watched failing, in tests/checks/requests-inbox.sh: `systemd/harness-requests.path` has `DirectoryNotEmpty=` or `PathExistsGlob=` on the requests directory, `Unit=harness-requests.service` and `WantedBy=default.target`; `systemd/harness-requests.service` has `Type=oneshot` and an `ExecStart=` ending in `bin/harness requests`; when `command -v systemd-analyze` succeeds, `systemd-analyze --user verify systemd/harness-requests.path systemd/harness-requests.service` exits 0 with no `error` line (the check copies both into $T with ExecStart's path rewritten to this checkout), otherwise the check passes and prints `skipped: no systemd-analyze` after its PASS line.
The check runs `harness requests` with `XDG_CONFIG_HOME=$T/cfg` and asserts that `$T/cfg` holds no `systemd` directory afterwards: the harness installs nothing.

`journal/decisions/2026-10-22-request-inbox.md` exists (title, provenance, finding · choice · rejected): the directory and its mode, the two verbs, the validation, the result and log files, the backup window, the path unit instead of the queue runner, the defaults (no third verb, no batching, a continue for a live run accepted as today) marked `*default*`, rejected: n8n committing to INBOX.md through the GitHub API (a write token in n8n, races with the driver's commits), the queue runner as the consumer (it exits when the queue is empty), a third verb; README.md's Steering section (`## Steering`) gets the request-inbox paragraph with the two install commands (`systemctl --user link …` and `systemctl --user enable --now harness-requests.path`) and the `requests/done/<id>.json` result; docs/architecture.md §3 names lib/requests.sh and lib/requests.mjs, §4 `requests/` (pending, done, rejected, requests.log, .lock), §7 Guards the validation and the backup window.

`bash tests/run.sh requests-inbox` ends with every check passing (its `N/N checks passed` line); every new name is in tests/fixtures/check-names.txt (LC_ALL=C sorted; a fast file's in check-names-fast.txt too).
`bash tests/run.sh --tier fast` ends with every check passing (its `N/N checks passed` line); the suite is green.

features.description: Review + simplify of A3: an Opus reviewer reads the milestone diff from a file and answers the hard questions (no request text can reach a shell, no path escapes the state root, a duplicate or half-written request is never run twice or rejected early); Critical/Important findings fixed RED→GREEN; simplifications applied; the decision file completed; docs as built.
steps: The milestone diff is written to a file (`git diff $(git merge-base HEAD origin/main) -- lib bin tests systemd docs journal README.md > $HARNESS_SCRATCH/A3.diff`) and read by an Opus subagent, one round (a second only if the first finds something Critical), which answers with file and line: that `text` and `brief` reach `harness answer` and `queue add` only as argv elements (every expansion quoted, no `eval`, `bash -c`, `printf %b` or here-string on them), that `run` and `id` can name no path outside `requests/` or the state root (the regexes applied before any path is built), that a request is processed at most once under concurrent `harness requests` (the lock, the `done/` check inside it, the rename) and that a half-written file is never rejected before its 10 s grace has passed; its findings (Critical, Important, Minor, each with file, line and what was done) are in `docs/plans/2026-11-07-A3-review.md`.

Every Critical and Important finding is fixed with a failing test first (a unit test in tests/unit/requests.test.mjs for a pure branch, a check in tests/checks/requests-inbox.sh for a CLI behaviour) and then green; simplification passes are applied; `bash -n` passes on every shell file A3 touched and `node --check` on every `.mjs`.

`journal/decisions/2026-10-22-request-inbox.md` is complete (finding, choice with every default marked `*default*`, rejected as docs/specs/2026-10-22-n8n-events.md §A4 lists them), and docs/architecture.md (§3, §4, §7 and the command list naming `harness requests`) and README.md (the Steering paragraph with both install commands and what Michael sees back on the card) describe A3 as built.
`bash tests/run.sh` (in the background, a timeout of at least 1,500,000 ms) ends with every check passing (its `N/M checks passed` line with N = M); the suite is green.

`journal/decisions/2026-10-22-event-hook-ntfy-fallback.md`, `journal/decisions/2026-10-22-context-bundle-glossary.md` and `journal/decisions/2026-10-22-request-inbox.md` exist, each with title, provenance, finding · choice · rejected, and no file under journal/decisions/ is numbered; the three are cited from docs/architecture.md.
